 There are several teams playing the second night of a back-to-back on Monday, including the Detroit Pistons, Los Angeles Lakers, New Orleans Pelicans and Dallas Mavericks. That could change how we go about this slate, especially if some star players end up sitting out.

 Dew’s Review: Want a crazy stat? NBA underdogs of eight or more points are 0-36 straight up in the 2026-27 season. Philadelphia, Dallas, Boston, Minnesota and Miami all won as 7.5-point favorites or more on Sunday, and there are a bunch of big favorites on Monday night. I also have to mention the now 9-2 Los Angeles Lakers, who are in first place in the Western Conference and rode a huge Austin Reaves game with Luka Doncic (back) sidelined to beat the Detroit Pistons and their No. 1 defense. So far, so good with the L.A. offseason building this team around Doncic and Reaves.

 Peter’s Point: Will Steph Curry and the Warriors keep it going? Golden State has won seven games in a row and is 5-1 at home heading into Monday’s game against the New Orleans Pelicans, who are playing the second night of a back-to-back. Curry and Co. rank sixth in the NBA in offensive rating this season, and they’ve covered the spread in seven of 10 games. It may be possible for this team to stay afloat in the West long enough for Jimmy Butler to return and make a real push for a top-six seed in the second half of the season.

 The Cavs are off to a 5-5 start this season, and they are just 16th in the league in net rating. It’s certainly not what Kenny Atkinson wanted to see from his team after an Eastern Conference Finals appearance in the 2025-26 campaign, but the Cavs are in a great spot on the road against the Charlotte Hornets on Monday.

 Charlotte has taken a major step back with LaMelo Ball now in Minnesota, ranking dead last in the league in offensive rating while averaging just 96.3 points per game.
